subject: System Design
title: Slack's Real-Time Messaging
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Slack's Real-Time Messaging.

hook.text: You type a message in Slack and your coworker sees it instantly. WebSocket connections keep the channel open.

buildup.text: Slack maintains a persistent WebSocket connection between your client and the server for real-time message delivery.

discovery.text: When you send a message, the server stores it and fans it out to all WebSocket connections in the channel.

twist.text: A company with 100,000 employees means 100,000 WebSocket connections. Each connection consumes memory on the server.

climax.text: Slack uses a gateway layer to multiplex connections and a pub/sub system to route messages to the right gateways.

punchline.text: WebSockets for real time, pub/sub for routing at scale.

quiz.question: How does Slack deliver messages in real time?
options: Persistent WebSocket connections deliver messages instantly to connected clients
Clients poll the server every second
